    Lemma 8.8 for bound quiver algebras #

    lem:dimension-infinity (local-ray-geometry.tex): "Let kQ/(ρ_1, …, ρ_t) be a finite-dimensional bound quiver algebra, with each relation between radical paths with specified endpoints. For a nonzero dimension vector d, put D = Σ_v d_v², N = Σ_{a : v → w} d_v d_w, F = Σ_i d_{source(ρ_i)} d_{target(ρ_i)}. If N − F ≥ D, the algebra is representation-infinite."

    The algebra kQ/(ρ) is the category algebra of the relation category kQ/(ρ) (path-order product). A point x of the representation space (matrices on the arrows) gives the arrow maps of a representation; the relations evaluate to the matrices relMat x i, whose entries are F polynomials in the coordinates (relP), vanishing at 0 (the relations have no length-zero part) and stable under ∏ GL_{d v} (relMat_act). A point of their zero set gives a functor kQ/(ρ) → Mod k (Φ), hence a right module of dimension Σ d_v (repObj), and isomorphic modules come from conjugate points (conj_of_iso). Finite representation type would give finitely many orbits, contradicting OrbitDim.orbits_not_finite (not_isRepresentationFinite_bound).

                                              Lemma 8.8 (lem:dimension-infinity): let kQ/(ρ₁, …, ρ_t) be a finite-dimensional bound quiver algebra (the category algebra of the relation category, path-order product), each relation ρ_i : s_i → t_i a combination of paths of positive length.
